description:
## Why
Elixir raises `UndefinedFunctionError` with `message: nil` and `reason: nil`. `UndefinedFunctionError.message/1` builds the text when it is asked for. With `reason: nil` it checks whether the module is loaded, and chooses "is undefined (module X is not available)" or "is undefined or private". So `e.message` is `nil` and `Exception.message(e)` is the text.

fz fills the field instead. `runtime/src/failure.rs` `raise_undefined_function` formats the three wordings in Rust and stores them in `message`. `src/ir_interp/backend.rs` calls the same function, so all three paths share it. A program that reads `e.message` prints the text on fz and an empty line on Elixir. Fixture 00869 met this and reads `Exception.message(e)` instead.

The wording lives twice: `lib/exceptions/undefined_function_error.fz` `undefined/4` also builds it.

## Finding (2026-11-15)
Raising with `message: nil` alone is not enough. `undefined/4` has no clause for `reason: nil` with a non-nil module and function, so `Exception.message(e)` would itself raise `FunctionClauseError`. Elixir answers that case with "is the module loaded?", asked at message time. fz has no run-time question for it. Whether a module exists is known only at the raise site, from the compile-time `modules_without` list on the backend `UndefinedFunction`.

## Options (owner decides)
A. Add the question Elixir asks: `Code.ensure_loaded?/1`, backed by the set of modules the program defines. `message/1` gains the `reason: nil` clause that asks it. The runtime raises with `message: nil` and the Rust wording is deleted. This is faithful to Elixir, and it adds a run-time module table, which needs a proof of necessity and a page.
B. Leave the raise as it is and record the difference in the exceptions docs.

## Signal (A)
A fixture with `# oracle: self` prints `e.message` of each miss (`nil` on all three) next to `Exception.message(e)`, and its golden matches Elixir. 00869 and the uncaught banner print the same text on run, interp and build.
title: A call that finds no function raises UndefinedFunctionError with message nil, as Elixir does
